extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers, program/study-section staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing NIH's simplified peer review framework for evaluating grant applications, including the reduced set of scored criteria, scoring conventions, narrative expectations, and additional (unscored) review considerations reviewers must attend to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A single overall impact score that reflects the reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the project, if supported, will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assign an overall impact score on the standard 1–9 NIH scale and summarize the major strengths and weaknesses that led to that score; the overall impact is a synthesis across the scored criteria rather than an additional independent criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the Research Question
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored criterion asking whether the application addresses an important problem or critical barrier in the field and the potential for the proposed work to change scientific concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, or preventative interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess relevance and potential transformative impact; consider whether outcomes would advance knowledge or practice. Include concise strengths and weaknesses that bear on importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored criterion combining assessment of scientific rigor, quality of conceptual framework/design/methods, attention to reproducibility, and the feasibility of the approach given the proposed timeline and preliminary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate experimental design, statistical plans, reproducibility practices (e.g., blinding, controls, sample-size justification), contingency plans, and whether methods are appropriate and likely to succeed. Note major methodological risks and whether they are mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise, Team, and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Scored criterion evaluating the investigators' qualifications, team composition and complementarity, institutional support, and availability of necessary resources and environment to accomplish the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider PI and key personnel track records, team breadth for interdisciplinary projects, mentoring/training where appropriate, and whether the institutional environment and available resources are sufficient. Cite strengths/weaknesses (e.g., missing expertise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring conventions (numeric 1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scoring range used for the overall impact and each scored criterion, where lower numbers indicate stronger reviews (1 = exceptional, 9 = poor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should use the full 1–9 scale, avoid assigning scores without explanatory narrative, and ensure scores are supported by the listed strengths and weaknesses. The page emphasizes consistency and use of the scale to discriminate levels of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths-and-weaknesses narrative requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must provide concise written critiques that identify the key strengths and weaknesses of the application that justify scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives should map to the scored criteria (importance, rigor/feasibility, expertise/team/resources) and be specific and actionable where possible. Avoid generic comments; list major weaknesses that could be addressed and major strengths that support high scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (protections for human subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scored consideration to evaluate protections for human subjects, risk/benefit, and whether proposed protections are adequate and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should comment if human subjects protections are inadequate or raise ethical/regulatory concerns; such issues do not receive a separate numeric score but can influence overall impact and funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (inclusion of women, minorities, and children)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scored consideration to assess inclusion plans and justification for any exclusion of demographic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether inclusion plans are appropriate and whether the application provides a rationale when groups are not included or when inclusion is not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (vertebrate animals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scored consideration of the appropriateness of use of vertebrate animals, including justification, protections, and plans for humane care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag inadequate justification, lack of appropriate oversight, or welfare issues; such concerns should be documented in the critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (biohazards/select agents and safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scored evaluation of biosafety and security considerations for proposed work involving hazardous agents or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note biosafety risks or insufficient mitigation; deficiencies should be recorded in the written critique even though they are not assigned a numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (resource sharing and data management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scored assessment of plans for sharing data, resources, and other outputs (e.g., data management and sharing plan, resource-sharing plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the presence and adequacy of plans; lack of an adequate plan may be noted as a weakness but typically is not scored separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration (authentication of key biological/chemical resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scored consideration asking whether applicants plan to authenticate key biological/chemical resources (e.g., cell lines, antibodies) when applicable to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note whether authentication steps are described and adequate, and record deficiencies in the critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and period of support – reviewer commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance that reviewers may comment on whether the requested budget and project period are appropriate to the scope, but budget is not a primary scored criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If budgetary requests are unreasonable or materially affect feasibility, reviewers should document concerns in their critiques rather than use budget as a scored criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and mapping from prior criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction that the simplified framework replaces the prior five scored criteria by consolidating and clarifying reviewer focus, and guidance on how to map legacy concerns (e.g., Innovation, Approach) into the new criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are told how prior criterion elements (such as innovation) should be considered within the new rubric (for example, innovation may inform 'importance' or 'rigor/feasibility'), and to avoid double-counting issues across criteria.
